name: Tapinarof

lead: Tapinarof (Vtama) is a prescription cream that clears the visible red, scaly plaques of psoriasis and eczema, so skin looks clearer and smoother. It is steroid-free and approved in the US for plaque psoriasis in adults and atopic dermatitis in adults and children aged 2 and older.

It activates the aryl hydrocarbon receptor in skin cells, which lab studies link to less inflammation and better barrier proteins; the label says the exact mechanism is unknown. Two phase 3 trials in plaque psoriasis were published in 2021, and a phase 2b trial reported efficacy in atopic dermatitis. Seborrheic dermatitis is described as under study, with no trial found in the sources reviewed.

paras: It is a 1% cream applied to affected patches as directed by a prescriber, as an ongoing treatment for the skin condition rather than a cosmetic. People use it where plaques show, and results build over weeks of regular use.
Label-listed reactions in psoriasis include folliculitis, nasopharyngitis, contact dermatitis and headache. Human pregnancy data are insufficient. It is prescription only.

angle.text: Tapinarof clears the visible plaques and redness of psoriasis and eczema, leaving skin clearer and smoother. It works by activating the AhR receptor in skin cells, which lowers inflammation. Phase 3 trials support its psoriasis use.

lead: Tapinarof (brand name Vtama) is a 1% topical cream and an aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) agonist. The US FDA label lists it for plaque psoriasis in adults and atopic dermatitis in adults and children aged 2 and older.[1] Its mechanism in these conditions is described on the label as unknown, although laboratory work shows it binds and activates AhR in skin cells.[1][2]

Two phase 3 trials in plaque psoriasis were published in 2021,[3] and a phase 2b trial in atopic dermatitis reported efficacy in adolescents and adults.[4] Seborrheic dermatitis is described as under study, but no trial for it appears in the sources reviewed.

paras: Per the US label, Vtama is indicated for plaque psoriasis in adults and for atopic dermatitis in adults and pediatric patients 2 years and older.[1] Grokipedia reports FDA approval for psoriasis in May 2022 and for atopic dermatitis in December 2024.[5]

Tapinarof is a naturally derived compound that binds and activates AhR, and its anti-inflammatory properties in mice and human skin were shown to depend on that activation.[2] Reviews describe AhR activity as strengthening skin barrier function and increasing filaggrin expression.[6]

Two phase 3 vehicle-controlled trials in plaque psoriasis were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021,[3] with a long-term extension of 763 adults registered.[7] A phase 2 dose-finding study and a phase 2b trial evaluated the cream in atopic dermatitis.[4][8] Registered studies include pediatric maximal-use work and small studies in cutaneous lupus and palmoplantar keratoderma.[9][10][11]

In plaque psoriasis the most common adverse reactions on the label (incidence of 1 percent or more) were folliculitis, nasopharyngitis, contact dermatitis, headache, pruritus and influenza. Human pregnancy data are insufficient to assess risk.[1]

timeline.event: Study identifies AhR activation as tapinarof's mechanism.[2]
US approval for plaque psoriasis (per Grokipedia).[5]
US approval for atopic dermatitis (per Grokipedia).[5]
